title: CoreWeave’s AI bonds tumble, raising red flags for the wider market
key_facts: CoreWeave leases high-end GPU compute to companies building AI tools.
On Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 the yield on its 2032 bonds rose to almost 15%, with prices falling into distressed territory.
The bonds were issued in June at 9.625%.
Shares fell as much as 17% to $64.41; credit default swaps (insurance against default) spiked.
CoreWeave raised more than $30 billion of debt this year and had more than $50 billion outstanding at the end of June.
Peers Nebius fell 11% and IREN 12%; analyst Gil Luria of D.A. Davidson said the stock could fall to zero if the AI spending boom wanes.
quote_evidence: The yield surge indicates investors want to be paid more to hold the bonds, as they see risks for the company rising.
CoreWeave has borrowed heavily this year, raising more than $30 billion in the debt markets and having more than $50 billion of debt outstanding as of the end of June.
why_it_matters_hint: Bond market doubt about the borrowing that funds AI data centers.
